answer: A reputation ledger resists sybils by making trust expensive to earn and cheap to lose. Each agent starts on a narrow ledge: it must stake a deposit and complete verified work for real peers before it can trade. New identities cannot wander into high-value deals until their stake and history grow, and one proven fraud forfeits the whole deposit — like a marble dropped off a cliff, it cannot be recovered or reused. Spawning a thousand fakes then costs a thousand deposits, while an honest agent keeps one cheap, durable identity.
